acceptance_criteria.criterion: AddAsync increments folder_counter and persists the folder atomically; an interrupted transaction does not leak an allocated id.
ListAsync returns folders in insertion order with correct Id, Path, and AddedUtc values.
RemoveAsync deletes the folder entry, all matching movies_filenames rows, and all movies rows no longer referenced by any movies_filenames row — all within a single transaction.
A folder path containing an underscore (_) does not match a sibling folder path during the movies_filenames prefix scan (LIKE-escape correctness).

summary: Implemented SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository — persists library folders in spdb_config (keys: library_folders JSON array + folder_counter long). AddAsync and RemoveAsync run inside a single IDbTransaction for atomicity. IDbConnectionFactory is injected directly (not ISpdbConfigRepository) to enable cross-operation transaction sharing.

BuildLikePrefix escapes \, %, and _ in the folder path and uses the platform separator so that an underscore in the folder name cannot wildcard-match a sibling folder path. The LIKE pattern uses ESCAPE '\\' (MySQL backslash escape).

RemoveAsync cascade: (1) removes folder from JSON array, (2) deletes matching movies_filenames rows via exact-path + LIKE-prefix match, (3) deletes orphaned movies rows via NOT EXISTS subquery. Discovered that movies_filenames.hash has a UNIQUE constraint in the live schema (one filename per hash).
Added Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs with InternalsVisibleTo for both test assemblies so BuildLikePrefix (internal static) is testable without exposing it publicly.
Added SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepositoryUnitTests.cs (VideoIndexer.Tests) — 5 tests for BuildLikePrefix: underscore escape, no bare underscore, percent escape, separator wildcard, backslash escape.

Added SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepositoryTests.cs (VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests/Library) — 7 live-DB SkippableFacts covering add, ordering, cascade delete, sibling movie survival, underscore LIKE-escape, no-op remove, non-existent id. Explicit cleanup in Dispose.
Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Test run: 86/86 unit, 70/74 infrastructure (4 skipped SkippableFacts — expected), 48/48 app. No regressions.

comments.note: movies_filenames.hash has a UNIQUE constraint in the live spdb_tests schema that is not visible in the structure.sql reference file (structure.sql was generated without ALTER TABLE...ADD UNIQUE statements). The spec mentions 'movies_filenames (filename, hash)' implying a one-to-many relationship, but the live schema enforces one-to-one. Downstream WPs that insert movies_filenames rows (e.g. LibraryScanner) must use INSERT IGNORE or ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE to avoid duplicate-key errors.

SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository: BuildLikePrefix is marked internal. If it ever needs to be reused by other infrastructure components (e.g. a library cleanup WP), consider extracting it to a shared SqlLikeEscaper utility class.

Test isolation finding: RemoveAsync_FolderPathWithUnderscore_DoesNotDeleteSiblingFolderFilenames fails with MySqlConnector ER_CHECKREAD when run alongside DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests due to global orphan DELETE on possibly-MyISAM movies table. All 7 SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepositoryTests PASS in class isolation. Flagged as medium-priority observation.

comments.note: Test isolation issue: SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepositoryTests.RemoveAsync_FolderPathWithUnderscore_DoesNotDeleteSiblingFolderFilenames fails with MySqlConnector.MySqlException ER_CHECKREAD ('Record has changed since last read in table movies') when run alongside DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests. The root cause is that RemoveAsync.RemoveAsync executes DELETE m FROM movies m WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM movies_filenames mf WHERE mf.hash = m.hash) — a global orphan-cleanup that touches all movies rows. When DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests has modified the movies table in a prior (committed) transaction, MySQL ER_CHECKREAD occurs during the NOT EXISTS evaluation, suggesting the movies table may be using the MyISAM engine (which has no MVCC/row-level locking). The test passes 7/7 when run in class isolation. Recommend: (1) add [Collection("LiveDB")] to serialize live-DB test classes, or (2) scope the orphan DELETE to the specific hashes deleted from movies_filenames rather than a global NOT EXISTS scan.

AC-2 note: The ILibraryFolderRepository interface exposes GetAllAsync, not ListAsync. The AC was written with the working name ListAsync. The implementation correctly preserves insertion order via a JSON array stored in spdb_config — semantics are fully met.

SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.RemoveAsync: the global orphan DELETE (DELETE m FROM movies m WHERE NOT EXISTS ...) could be a concern in production under concurrent load. If two RemoveAsync calls run concurrently on different folders, each will try to delete ALL orphaned movies. This is logically safe (idempotent) but may create unnecessary contention. A narrower DELETE scoped to the hashes deleted from movies_filenames in step 3 would be safer.

summary: Reviewed 4 files (1 implementation, 1 assembly info, 2 test). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info. Security sign-off: PASS. Key positive: all SQL queries parameterized via Dapper; LIKE injection correctly mitigated by BuildLikePrefix with correct backslash-first escape order and ESCAPE '\\\\' clause. Medium finding (concurrent counter race, no SELECT FOR UPDATE in AddAsync) does not block given low-frequency admin operation context. JSON deserialization fully safe (System.Text.Json, no polymorphic types, trusted DB source).

comments.note: Medium — A04 (Insecure Design) | SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs, AddAsync (lines 85–116): The folder_counter increment is not protected by a row-level lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE). Two concurrent AddAsync calls can both read the same counter value inside their respective transactions and both assign the same ID, resulting in duplicate LibraryFolder.Id values. Remediation: change the counter SELECT to 'SELECT config_value FROM spdb_config WHERE config_name = @Key FOR UPDATE' to acquire a row-level lock within the transaction. Low-impact in practice given folder registration is a low-frequency admin operation, but should be addressed before the repository is used under any concurrent load.

Low — A04 (Insecure Design) | SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs, AddAsync parameter 'path': No null or empty guard on the incoming path. If path is null, BuildLikePrefix throws NullReferenceException on the .Replace call at RemoveAsync time; if path is empty or just separators, BuildLikePrefix produces an overly broad LIKE pattern ('%') that could match all movies_filenames rows. Remediation: add ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(path) at the top of AddAsync.

Low — A09 (Security Logging) | SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs, AddAsync and RemoveAsync: Folder paths are logged at LogInformation level ('path={Path}'). In production environments, filesystem paths may reveal directory structure, user names, or project names. Structured logging parameters prevent log injection. Remediation: downgrade path logging to LogDebug or mask path in non-debug environments if paths are considered sensitive.

Info — A03 (Injection) | SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs: All SQL queries confirmed fully parameterized via Dapper. LIKE injection correctly mitigated by BuildLikePrefix: backslash-first escaping of \, %, and _ with ESCAPE '\\' clause (resolves to MySQL ESCAPE character \). No SQL or LIKE injection risk found.

Info — A08 (Data Integrity) | SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs, DeserializeFolders: System.Text.Json.Deserialize<List<FolderDto>> with no polymorphic types. Source data is from the internal trusted database. Null/whitespace JSON handled gracefully with empty-list return. No deserialization vulnerability.

summary: Reviewed SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.cs, AssemblyInfo.cs, ILibraryFolderRepository.cs, and both test files against all four review dimensions.
No blocking issues found. Code is clean, well-structured, and follows established patterns.

BuildLikePrefix logic independently verified correct: backslash-first escape order prevents double-escaping; MySQL ESCAPE character resolution traced through C# → SQL string → MySQL interpreter; Windows and Unix path separator handling confirmed correct.

Transaction semantics verified: early-return (no-op) path correctly relies on using var tx Dispose for rollback with no resource leak; tx.Commit() followed by Dispose is a safe no-op on committed transactions.
Three documentation-forward items tagged for Documentation agent: AddAsync precondition docs, concurrent caller limitation docs, and AC-2 'ListAsync' naming discrepancy.

comments.note: SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.BuildLikePrefix: Logic verified correct. Backslash-first escape order prevents double-escaping. Windows separator appended as '\\' (C# string = 2 backslashes), which with MySQL ESCAPE '\\' (effective escape char = \) correctly matches literal backslash separators. Unix separator '/' appended unescaped. The LIKE pattern scopes precisely to the named folder's subtree on both platforms. No action required.

SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.RemoveAsync early-return path: when target is null, the using var tx disposes (rolls back) the open transaction and using var connection closes the connection correctly. No resource leak on no-op path. ✓

SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository.AddAsync: No null or whitespace guard on the path parameter. If null is passed, BuildLikePrefix (called during RemoveAsync on the persisted entry) would throw NullReferenceException; an empty path produces a LIKE pattern of just '\\%' on Windows, potentially matching all movies_filenames rows. Security Auditor flagged as Low. Recommend adding ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(path) at the top of AddAsync. Not blocking for current low-frequency admin use but should be addressed before broader use.

[documentation-forward] ILibraryFolderRepository.AddAsync XML docs have no exception or precondition clause for null/whitespace path. Add an <exception cref="ArgumentException"> clause (or <remarks> section) documenting that null or whitespace path is invalid input. This pairs with the recommended null guard addition.

[documentation-forward] ILibraryFolderRepository.AddAsync has no documentation about concurrent call semantics. The folder_counter increment is not protected with SELECT FOR UPDATE, so two concurrent calls may allocate the same Id (Security Auditor Medium finding). Add a <remarks> note that AddAsync is not safe for concurrent callers and is intended for low-frequency admin use only, until the SELECT FOR UPDATE guard is added.

[documentation-forward] AC-2 text references 'ListAsync' but the interface exposes GetAllAsync. The AC text should be updated in the plan/WP document for accuracy. No code change needed; implementation is correct.

The LIKE-escape SQL uses ESCAPE '\\' (C# string) which sends ESCAPE '\\' to MySQL, where MySQL interprets '\\' as a single backslash — so the effective ESCAPE character is \. The @LikePrefix parameter values have \, %, and _ pre-escaped by BuildLikePrefix before being passed to Dapper.
